claims.text: A multiscale defect-incorporating computational approach can predict the thermal conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen within 10% of measurements over 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The proposed approach will be more accurate than conventional analytical methods based on perfect crystalline models.
The target material is polycrystalline HfNbTaTiZr with approximately 1 wt.% oxygen and a stable microstructure.
The modeling framework explicitly represents point-defect scattering.
The modeling framework explicitly represents sublattice disorder.
The proposed validation covers 0–200 K and 300–1200 K in an inert or vacuum atmosphere at approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Oxygen point defects alter phonon transport pathways in HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen point defects and random lattice-site occupation alter electron transport pathways in HfNbTaTiZr.
Representing oxygen-defect scattering and compositional disorder captures scattering mechanisms omitted by perfect-crystal DFT or simplified analytical approaches.
Capturing defect and disorder scattering will reduce systematic errors in predicted phonon scattering and yield conductivity predictions within 10% of measurements.
Existing analytical models can deviate by 20–30% from experimental conductivity data for defective multielement alloys.
The approach remains robust for HfNbTaTiZr with less than 3 wt.% oxygen and similar single-phase microstructures.
Higher defect concentrations or phase transformations may require model recalibration or extension.
Accuracy above the tested 1 wt.% oxygen level or in more complex phase structures is undetermined.
A deviation greater than 10% at any measured temperature in either specified range would falsify the hypothesis.
